passages.scripture: Rid yourselves, therefore, of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.

lines.text: So get rid of all malice — all ill will toward others.
Get rid of all deceit — lies and trickery.
Get rid of all hypocrisy — pretending to be good.
Get rid of all envy — resenting what others have.
Get rid of all slander — speaking evil of others.

passages.scripture: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation, now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.

lines.text: You are like newborn babies.
Crave pure spiritual milk — the pure word of God.
So by this milk you may grow up spiritually.
This growth leads to your salvation.
The Lord is good.
You have already tasted this for yourself.

passages.scripture: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight, you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

lines.text: You come to Jesus, the living stone.
People rejected this stone.
But in God's sight Jesus is chosen and precious.
You also are like living stones.
God is building you into a spiritual house — God's temple.
God is making you a holy priesthood.
As priests you offer spiritual sacrifices.
Your sacrifices are acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

lines.text: Zion is the holy city of God.
Behold, God lays a stone there.
This stone is chosen and precious.
This stone is the cornerstone — the most important stone.
Anyone who believes in this stone will never be put to shame.
Scripture says that God says this.

passages.scripture: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,” and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.

lines.text: So to you who believe, this stone — Jesus — is precious.
But some people do not believe.
The builders rejected this stone.
But this stone has become the cornerstone.
This stone also makes people stumble.
It is a rock that makes them fall — just as the Scriptures foretold.
They stumble because they disobey the word.
And they were appointed to this stumbling.

passages.scripture: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

lines.text: But you are a chosen people.
You are a royal priesthood.
You are a holy nation.
You are God's own special possession.
God called you out of darkness.
He brought you into His wonderful light.
So proclaim God's glorious virtues.

passages.scripture: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

lines.text: Once you were not a people.
But now you are the people of God.
Once you had not received mercy.
But now you have received mercy.

passages.scripture: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.

lines.text: Beloved, I urge you.
You are foreigners and exiles in this world.
So abstain from the desires of the flesh — your sinful cravings.
These desires wage war against your soul.

passages.scripture: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.

lines.text: Live honorably among the Gentiles — the unbelievers around you.
They may slander you as evildoers.
But they will see your good deeds.
And they will glorify God when He visits us.

passages.scripture: Submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human institution, whether to the king as the supreme authority, or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.

lines.text: Submit to every human authority for the Lord's sake.
Submit to the king as the highest authority.
And submit to governors and everyone else sent by the king.
Governors punish those who do wrong.
And governors praise those who do right.

passages.scripture: For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.

lines.text: Some people are foolish.
These foolish people are ignorant.
By doing good, you silence their ignorance.
This is God's will.

passages.scripture: Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

lines.text: Live in freedom.
But do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil.
Instead, live as servants of God.

passages.scripture: Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king.

lines.text: Honor everyone.
Love the family of believers.
Fear God.
Honor the king.

passages.scripture: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.

lines.text: Servants, submit to your masters.
Submit with all respect.
Some masters are good and gentle.
Submit not only to them.
Submit even to masters who are unreasonable.

passages.scripture: For if anyone endures the pain of unjust suffering because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.

lines.text: Suppose someone endures the pain of unjust suffering.
They do this because they are mindful of God.
This finds favor with God.

passages.scripture: How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.

lines.text: Suppose you are beaten for doing wrong, and you endure it.
That is no credit to you.
But suppose you suffer for doing good, and you endure it.
This finds favor with God.

passages.scripture: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps: “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”

lines.text: God has called you to this.
Christ also suffered for you.
Christ left you an example.
So follow in His footsteps.
Christ committed no sin.
No deceit was found in His mouth.

passages.scripture: When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.

lines.text: When people insulted Christ, He did not insult them back.
When Christ suffered, He made no threats.
Instead, Christ entrusted Himself to God.
For God judges justly.

passages.scripture: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”

lines.text: Christ Himself bore our sins in His own body on the cross.
So we might die to sin.
And live for righteousness.
By His wounds you are healed.

passages.scripture: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

lines.text: You were like sheep going astray.
But now you have returned to the Shepherd, Jesus.
Jesus is the Guardian of your souls.
